action: Prescribe chronic anticoagulant therapy for HF patients with AF and elevated CHA2DS2-VASc score
action_detail: Patients with chronic HF with permanent/persistent/paroxysmal AF and CHA2DS2-VASc score >=2 (men) or >=3 (women) should receive chronic anticoagulant therapy for stroke prevention
source_text: Patients with chronic HF with permanent-persistent-paroxysmal AF and a CHA2DS2-VASc score of >= 2 (for men) and >= 3 (for women) should receive chronic anticoagulant therapy. (Class I, LOE A)

action: Prefer DOAC over warfarin for anticoagulation in HF with AF
action_detail: For patients with chronic HF with AF, DOAC is recommended over warfarin in eligible patients. DOACs do not need routine anticoagulation monitoring or dose adjustment, have fewer drug interactions, and have an improved benefit-risk profile compared with warfarin
source_text: For patients with chronic HF with permanent-persistent-paroxysmal AF, DOAC is recommended over warfarin in eligible patients. (Class I, LOE A)

action: Monitor INR for warfarin therapy in HF patients with AF
action_detail: When warfarin is used for anticoagulation in HF patients with AF (when favored because of other indications, cost, or drug-drug interactions), routine anticoagulation monitoring with INR is required. Therapeutic INR range is 2.0-3.0. This is implied by the guideline contrasting DOACs (which do not need routine anticoagulation monitoring) with warfarin.
source_text: These drugs [DOACs] do not need routine anticoagulation monitoring or dose adjustment... Anticoagulation may be accomplished with DOAC or with warfarin when favored because of other indications, cost or drug-drug interactions.

action: Consider AF ablation for symptom improvement in HF patients
action_detail: For patients with HF and symptoms caused by AF, AF catheter ablation is reasonable to improve symptoms and quality of life. RCTs showed ablation may reduce hospitalizations and mortality compared with antiarrhythmic drugs or standard care
source_text: For patients with HF and symptoms caused by AF, AF ablation is reasonable to improve symptoms and QOL. (Class IIa, LOE B-R)

action: Consider AV nodal ablation with CRT implantation when rhythm control fails in AF with LVEF <=50%
action_detail: For patients with AF and LVEF <=50%, if rhythm control strategy fails or is not desired and ventricular rates remain rapid despite medical therapy, atrioventricular nodal ablation with implantation of a CRT device is reasonable. CRT is preferred over RV pacing in patients with reduced LVEF.
source_text: For patients with AF and LVEF <= 50%, if a rhythm control strategy fails or is not desired, and ventricular rates remain rapid despite medical therapy, atrioventricular nodal ablation with implantation of a CRT device is reasonable. (Class IIa, LOE B-R)

action: Consider anticoagulation for HF patients with AF even without additional CHA2DS2-VASc risk factors
action_detail: For patients with chronic HF and AF, chronic anticoagulant therapy is reasonable even for men and women without additional risk factors beyond HF itself, as HF is a hypercoagulable state and independent risk factor for stroke in AF

properties.context: HF patients even without additional CHA2DS2-VASc risk factors

source_text: For patients with chronic HF and permanent-persistent-paroxysmal AF, chronic anticoagulant therapy is reasonable for men and women without additional risk factors. (Class IIa, LOE B-NR)

action: Use specific DOAC agents for anticoagulation in HF with AF
action_detail: Several DOACs are available including factor Xa inhibitors apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban, and direct thrombin inhibitor dabigatran. In meta-analysis of 4 trials, DOACs more effectively reduced stroke/systemic embolism, major bleeding, and intracranial bleeding compared with warfarin, with no treatment heterogeneity by HF status.
source_text: Several DOAC are available, including the factor Xa inhibitors apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban, and the direct thrombin inhibitor dabigatran... DOAC more effectively reduced the rate of stroke or systemic embolism, major bleeding, and intracranial bleeding compared with warfarin.
